name: Dennis Mahoney
current_role: Disaster relief and community development worker
bio: Dennis Mahoney is an independent candidate for Pennsylvania's 3rd Congressional District whose career has focused on disaster relief and long-term development. In Philadelphia he works with businesses, nonprofits and faith groups on foster care prevention, food access and support for schools and educators.

platform.point: Phase benefits out gradually as income rises and update anti-poverty programs around mobility.
Expand affordable housing, support first-time buyers and build more homes near transit.
Improve transit, broadband and workforce training across neighborhoods.
Restore the expanded Child Tax Credit, protect food aid and make childcare cheaper.
Fix tangled property titles, fund home repairs and support small businesses.
Expand community-based healthcare access and keep a raise from costing families their coverage.

economy.evidence: General statement: calls for public investment in affordable housing, transit, broadband, workforce training and neighborhood small businesses.

welfare.evidence: Backs restoring the Child Tax Credit, protecting food assistance and cheaper childcare.

notes: Checked the campaign home, about, press and promises pages; the site has no stated positions on immigration, abortion, guns, foreign policy, energy, tech, schools or policing, and no press coverage was listed. Web search was unavailable in this round, so news and voter-guide coverage could not be checked.

name: Ken Block
bio: Ken Block is running for Governor of Rhode Island as an independent in 2026, his third bid for the office. He founded the Moderate Party of Rhode Island and was its 2010 nominee, then lost the 2014 Republican primary. A software engineer with a Dartmouth computer science degree, he founded companies that analyze government waste and fraud; he was born in Milford, Connecticut, and lives in Barrington.

platform.point: Veto a millionaires tax and lower state fees and taxes to reduce living costs.
Suspend the truck toll program and oppose tolls on cars.
Review every state agency and end spending on poorly managed projects.
Use state-owned property for affordable housing and require a housing impact note on legislation.
Overhaul RIDOT management and award contracts on merit.
Base judicial appointments on merit and take magistrate picks away from the General Assembly.
Audit every state-imposed charge on electric bills, cut unneeded ones and move others into the state budget, aiming for 25% lower bills.
Says law-abiding residents have a right to own firearms and that gun policy will not be a main focus of his term.

economy.evidence: Would veto a millionaire's tax and cut state costs rather than add taxes; wants lower state fees and taxes.

welfare.evidence: Proposes a New England regional health insurance marketplace and a review of Medicaid spending for impact; a general statement.

energy.evidence: Plans to audit state-imposed charges on electric bills, drop unneeded ones and move others into the state budget, aiming for 25% lower bills.

notes: Supports the right to own firearms but says gun policy won't be a focus, and doesn't campaign on abortion; one issue isn't enough to place him on personal freedom, so it stays blank.

name: Clayton Cuteri
bio: Clayton Cuteri is a software engineer and entrepreneur from Mount Pleasant who owns several businesses, including a social media company, and hosts a podcast. He co-founded the American Congress Party, a new national party, and serves as its secretary general. He is running as a write-in candidate.

platform.point: Lease unused federal land free to regenerative farmers, with part of the harvest given away and glyphosate banned.
Aims to curb rising homeowner insurance premiums in the Lowcountry.
Wants to make homes affordable for Lowcountry families.
Backs free medication as part of the American Congress Party platform.
Supports free education under his party's platform.
Favors eliminating the federal income tax and returning to the gold standard.
Wants to end heavy spending on foreign wars and redirect those resources home.
Repeal the Invention Secrecy Act, fund wave and kinetic energy research, and phase out nuclear power.

welfare.evidence: Party platform he promotes calls for free medication and free education.

foreign.evidence: Calls for ending spending on foreign wars and redirecting the money home.

energy.evidence: Calls for strict pollution enforcement, reforestation and new wave and kinetic energy sources while ending nuclear power.

education.evidence: Proposes free education at every level with higher teacher pay and a redesigned curriculum; he does not mention vouchers.

notes: His campaign site presents him as a write-in candidate of the American Congress Party, not an independent; its 13 policy pages were read. Economy stays null because he pairs ending the income tax and the Federal Reserve with free food, medicine and education, and no immigration, guns, abortion, policing or religion positions were found.

name: Brian Bengs
current_role: Veteran and former political science professor
bio: Brian Bengs is a retired Air Force lieutenant colonel and Navy veteran who taught political science at Northern State University in Aberdeen. He was the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in South Dakota in 2022 and is running as an independent in 2026, endorsed by the Forward Party.

platform.point: Raise taxes on the ultra-wealthy toward 1960s levels while lowering taxes for workers and small businesses.
Overhaul the health care system in stages to lower costs and widen access.
Ban stock trading by members of Congress, adopt a Supreme Court ethics code and limit senators to two terms.
Pair strong border security with expanded legal immigration to support economic growth.
Enforce antitrust law against corporate concentration in agriculture.
Guarantee consumers the right to repair products they own.
Protect Social Security and Medicare and oppose efforts to privatize them.
As a gun owner, backs the right to bear arms along with reasonable gun safety measures.

economy.evidence: Wants the ultra-wealthy taxed at 1960s-era levels and antitrust enforcement in agriculture.

welfare.evidence: General statement: pledges to protect Social Security and Medicare from privatization and to overhaul health care to widen access.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion access until viability, gun rights with reasonable safety measures, and LGBTQ acceptance.

immigration.evidence: Calls for strong border security together with more legal immigration.

tech.evidence: General statement: supports a consumer right to repair and criticizes data center incentives he says favor Big Tech.

notes: Read the campaign policy, values, issue-quiz and media pages, Wikipedia and a KOTA interview; his foreign policy page is a quiz without his answers, and no education, energy, policing or religion positions were found. The Commons photo was not used because its authorship is unclear.
